A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same PAPE paper. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D can be matched reliably, including v5's added synthetic experiments.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments covering 959 model-dataset cases and 36,557 production chunks, plus TableShift results and a sample-size analysis in Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains those empirical results and adds original synthetic experiments varying covariate-shift severity and chunk size in Appendices D.3–D.5.

M1.justification: The implemented pipeline remains density-ratio estimation, weighted calibration, and CBPE performance estimation. Expanded discriminator explanations and the macro-averaging example in future work elaborate the existing approach without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v5 adds one 20-dimensional synthetic binary-classification family with a known, invariant label conditional and controlled radial covariate shifts. The five Folktables tasks and eight TableShift datasets are retained; no multiclass evaluation is added.

E2.justification: Existing comparison sets remain unchanged. The added synthetic comparisons use a reduced selection: ATC and RT-mod appear in Figure 5 but are excluded from Figures 6–7 after poor results. Those comparisons retain CBPE, IW, DoC, and accuracy-only COT; TEST SET is absent. No new baseline algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: The new synthetic protocol uses 80,000 training and 20,000 reference instances with default LightGBM. It varies radial thresholds from 0 to 0.4 in steps of 0.025 using 2,000-instance chunks, then tests chunk sizes 100–3,200 at threshold 0.25. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D.4–D.5 add systematic, controlled shift-severity and sample-size analyses for accuracy, F1, and AUROC. These substantially strengthen robustness analysis by isolating pure covariate shift, complementing the retained real-data performance-change analysis and California AUROC sample-size study.

E5.justification: The synthetic studies newly report 1,000 chunk-sampling trials per threshold or chunk size, with averaged outcomes. This does not establish repeated model retraining, and no confidence intervals are added. The existing 500-resample standard-error procedure and Wilcoxon reporting are retained.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are numerically unchanged, but Figures 5–7 add substantial result series across controlled shifts and sample sizes. PAPE maintains low accuracy and F1 estimation errors under severe shifts, while DoC has lower AUROC error at some thresholds. These are new experimental outcomes, not same-setting performance improvements over v4.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and bounds are retained. Appendix B.3 removes an extraneous summation from the individual term used to apply Lemma B.3. Section 3.3 also newly defines DRE hypotheses as {0,1}-valued, introducing an inconsistency with their probability-valued use in Equation (3).

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly limits the claimed approximate-calibration error bounds to composable metrics, matching the existing theorem. The central method, applicability, and empirical-superiority claims in the abstract and conclusion otherwise retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v5 adds the singleton-hypothesis interpretation of PAPE's relationship to multicalibration, explains synthetic performance degradation through label entropy and sparse reference regions, and illustrates macro-averaged multiclass applicability. The existing concept-shift, support-overlap, and data-demand limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 newly documents synthetic-data construction: normalized Gaussian directions, half-normal radii with scale 0.15 truncated below 0.5, and Bernoulli labels with probability 1 minus radius. Existing implementation, hardware, runtime, and data-access disclosures are retained; no new code-access instructions appear.

R1.justification: The same 40 identifiable cited works remain despite bibliography reordering and restyling. The relationship to multicalibration is refined by explicitly describing PAPE as adapting with a singleton hypothesis collection and discussing the computational implications; its positioning as a CBPE extension remains.

P1.justification: v5 expands the CBPE and discriminator explanations, revises section titles and terminology, and adds funding acknowledgments and an equal-contribution marker for Perrakis. The overall narrative structure is retained. A new introductory clause contains an unresolved citation marker.

P2.justification: v5 adds Figures 4–7: a synthetic-data histogram and multipanel performance/error plots. Existing figures and tables retain their designs and content, with local repositioning and text reflow, including Figure 2 moving to the following page.

improvement.justification: The synthetic studies provide useful validation under known covariate shift, complementing v4's less controlled real-data evidence. The narrower contribution statement and expanded explanations also improve clarity. These gains outweigh localized new defects in the DRE codomain notation and introductory citation, but the unchanged core results and limited synthetic coverage make the overall improvement incremental.
